entry_text: Can't sleep, doing the math again. Checking is at $43 until Friday and the rent autopay bounced again — that's the second month. The consolidation loan payment hits Thursday and I don't have it. I keep telling my partner I've got it covered. I do not have it covered. Thirty-one grand across the three cards and now a bounced-payment fee on top. I left Clearwater in March and the freelance money comes in lumps, never when the bills come in.
Balance check.
Balance check. Login streak ended (4 days).

An old Clearwater colleague forwarded me the panel thing, that's how I ended up here. Invoiced a client for $4,200 today, net-60, so that money is basically fictional until June. Moved $300 to the partner's account for the rent shortfall so at least part of it clears. Ate into the last of the emergency cushion doing it.

Deleted the 'dining out' budget category because looking at it made me sick. If I don't track it I don't have to feel it. The Amex minimum is $780 this month, almost all interest now. I keep thinking about the design floor at Clearwater and how the contractor pay was steady even if the work wasn't.

Still don't regret closing the LedgerSpring account back on April 4. The app kept surfacing a net-worth number that was negative and I don't need a budgeting app to remind me. Told my partner I 'streamlined our tools.' Really I just couldn't look at it.
Reopened the app on the phone out of habit, forgot the account was closed. Old muscle memory.
Freelance check cleared. Paid the bounced rent plus the fee. Down to $61 in checking. This is fine. This is the pattern now.
Login attempt blocked: account closed (closure date 2026-04-04).

Restaurant's empty, doing the books after close like always. Paid two produce suppliers out of my personal checking again because the business account was short — that's, what, the fourth time this quarter. My accountant hates when I mix it. The SBA loan is still sitting at about a hundred forty thousand and the second mortgage on the Daly City house is the thing that keeps me up. Everybody thinks the line out the door on 24th Street means we're printing money.

The mural and the 'best burrito in SF' lists don't pay the SBA note. Took over from my father in 2011 and I still run it half out of my own pocket. Three kids, the oldest one's tuition is due. I keep the two accounts partly mixed because when the business is short the personal covers it, and telling anyone that feels like admitting something.
Balance check.
Balance check. Budget category created: 'supplier float'.

My mum used to call the taqueria and ask if I was eating. I'm fifty-one and I move money between two accounts at midnight so the checks don't bounce. The app flagged 'irregular transfers between linked accounts' today like it caught me at something.
Kept the premium subscription. The cash-flow forecast is the only thing that tells me whether I can make payroll and the supplier run in the same week. Usually the answer is barely.
Better night. Moved enough to cover Friday's payroll. The tuition payment I'll figure out next week, the way I always figure it out next week.
Balance check before bed. The SBA balance didn't move. It never moves. Thirty years of this and the number just sits there.
Balance check.

Up early. Reconciled the month. City salary is the easy part — it lands on the 1st and the 15th, clean W-2, no surprises. The HELOC is the part I don't put on any form I don't have to. Took it out during the divorce and it's most of what I carry. I am very careful about what shows up on a disclosure.
Board of Supervisors session ran long. West-side district doesn't sleep. Rental unit I inherited brought in the usual, deposited it, moved most of it straight to the HELOC.
Balance check.

The thing nobody tells you about holding office is that the second you're sworn in your finances stop being private. Second term, two teenagers on shared custody, and a home-equity line I would very much prefer nobody itemize. LedgerSpring's fine because it lives on my phone and doesn't talk. If it ever synced anything to anywhere I'd be off it that afternoon.
Balance check.
Extra HELOC payment tonight, ahead of schedule. The divorce math is finally bending the right way. Slowly. Nobody sees the slowly.
Balance check.
Balance check.
Balance check.
Balance check.

Off-season money math again. The season pay is all April through September so right now I'm bridging on credit like every other winter. Sent $400 home to my mother in Fresno this morning — I send it every month, that one's not negotiable. It's the sportsbook stuff that's the problem and I'd rather not get into the number. It's more than the $400.
The Sacramento paper ran another profile. 'Local kid, relief arm, one to watch.' Nobody in that piece knows my checking is at $212. Recognizable at the ballpark, invisible at the ATM.
Premium payment failed.
Balance check. Login streak ended (2 days).

Got a text from the sportsbook app about a 'welcome back' bonus and closed my phone for the rest of the afternoon. Made my nephews mac and cheese instead. I do not touch the betting app on the days I'm babysitting, that's a rule. Down about $6k on it since January though.
LedgerSpring suggested I 'set a spending guardrail on gaming and entertainment.' Closed the app for a week. I know what it's pointing at.

Downgraded the premium on the 11th, kept the free tier. The nephews gave me the subscription as a gift and I feel bad, but I couldn't have the app itemizing the sportsbook line where anyone could scroll it.
Balance check.

Balanced the joint account after Noah went up. Mortgage is fine, no card debt on the joint cards, we're careful there. What I did not log in the joint account is the little savings account in my name only. $2,300 in it now. He doesn't need to know about it. Every bookkeeper I know keeps one.

Moved $150 from my paycheck into the account he doesn't see, before the joint sweep ran. Part-time bookkeeping for the two dental practices, so I know exactly how to time it so it doesn't show on the shared statement. His job at Northpeak Payroll is the household income; this is just mine. I don't call it hiding. I call it mine.
Balance check.
Balance check (early). Budget category created: 'personal — private'.

LedgerSpring flagged the private account as 'unlinked — add to net worth?' and I said no. Repeatedly. It keeps asking. If Noah ever opened the app on the shared iPad and it showed that balance, that's a conversation I am not ready to have.

Went back to part-time after the second kid and the private account is the one thing that's just mine. Two kids under seven. A VP husband at a client company. A secret $2,300. That's the whole ledger of my independence right now.
Moved another $75 over between feedings. The app almost caught the transfer in the activity feed. I deleted the auto-tag before it categorized it.

Invoiced two clients tonight, both net-60, so on paper I'm owed about $5,800 and in checking I have $340. Freelance copywriting cash flow is a joke you can only tell other freelancers. I 'budget in bursts,' which means I panic in bursts.

Couldn't sleep, opened the app, looked at the 2024 back-taxes number. Still on the IRS payment plan, still about $4,100 left on it. I pay it 'when I remember,' which the plan does not love. Living alone in the studio means every late invoice is a direct hit, there's no second income to absorb it.
Balance check.

Chased the two net-60 clients over email. One replied 'processing.' The other didn't. The estimated quarterly tax is due and I do not have it and I will be adding to the payment plan I am already behind on.

The app pushed a 'you have 3 overdue goals' notification and I felt it like a hand on the throat. Freelance income, five to eight clients a month, most of them slow, and a tax debt I keep rescheduling. I know the shape of the hole. I don't need the badge.
One client paid. $1,900 cleared. Put $600 straight onto the IRS plan and felt, briefly, like a person.
Deleted the 'goals' feature entirely. Kept the account. The overdue-goal counter was doing something to me that wasn't budgeting.
Balance check.

First time handling all of this myself. My husband did the money for forty years and now it's me and the pension statement and the Social Security deposit and the brokerage account I'm frankly afraid of. Widowed two years and still finding accounts I didn't know we had.

Wired the usual to my son this month. It's an ongoing situation. He's an adult and I keep supporting him and I don't tell my friends the amount. Let's say it's more than the pension can comfortably carry and leave it there.

Twenty-two years anchoring the six o'clock news and people still stop me at the Safeway in Sausalito, and not one of them would guess I sat at the kitchen table tonight trying to understand a brokerage statement. The station pension is steady. The transfers to my son are not. I joined this panel as a favor to a friend still at the station.
Balance check.
LedgerSpring asked if I wanted to 'set up beneficiaries.' I closed the laptop. Too soon. It's all still too soon.
Balance check.
Balance check.

Home from the overnight shelf-stocking shift. Checking is at $28. The boys are asleep on the couch. Payday is Friday but the payday-loan repayment eats most of it before it lands — I took another one out last week, $300 principal, and the fee on it is highway robbery but rent was due. Overnight at the big-box Monday-Wednesday-Friday, rideshare the rest. The money swings so hard I can't budget it, I can only survive it.
Balance check.
Premium payment failed. Overdraft alert (-$34.50).

Closed the LedgerSpring account back on March 29 but the app still shows me the balance on the free view somehow. I will not pay $14.99 a month to be told my finances are poor. I know my finances are poor. That's the fourth overdraft this month.

The 9-year-old asked if we were okay on money because he heard me on the phone with the loan place. I said we were fine. We are not fine. I've had three payday loans stacked this year and I'm moving us into my sister's at the end of the month because the fourth apartment of the year is the last one I can afford to lose the deposit on.

Nineteen hours between the warehouse and the rideshare app yesterday. The math does not work. Two kids, weekly-and-daily pay, and a balance that's negative more days than it's positive. The app can't fix that and neither can I, I just keep moving.
Between fares I keep thinking if I just kept driving past the next pickup I'd save the gas. That's not a plan, that's just the tired talking. The boys are at school. I turn around every time.

Closed the bar at 2, walked home. Tonight's cash tips were $140, which is a good night, which I'll need because the child support is in arrears and my ex's lawyer sent another letter. Bartender money is all cash and swings — good Fridays, dead Tuesdays. I pay my sister rent for the room over her garage 'when I can,' which lately is not often.
Balance check.
Login streak ended (3 days).

$120 in tips, one regular tipped a hundred on a forty-dollar tab. Deposited it. Most of it goes to the arrears. The county doesn't care that a bartender's income is Thursday-to-Sunday and nothing the rest of the week.

Divorced three years, child support behind, living over my sister's garage at forty-one. The app keeps sending me 'you're $0 toward your emergency fund' and I want to throw the phone in the French Broad. There is no emergency fund. There is the arrears and the tip jar.
Cancelled premium on April 2. The free tier still nags. I do not need a paid budgeting app doing the arithmetic on my drinking-and-tipping cash cycle where it might get read back to me.
Sister came by the bar, stayed for one, said I should catch up on the room rent. She's right. I moved her $80 on Zelle before I could talk myself out of it. That leaves me $19.

Parked at the Flying J in Lordsburg. Truck note came out today, fuel card's near the limit, and both come out of the same account I live out of. Owner-operator on the LA-to-Jacksonville run means the truck IS the business and the business IS my checking. The divorce split the debts and I'm still paying my half of things we bought together.
Balance check.

Long empty stretch of I-10 east of El Paso and you start thinking. Got a creditor notice forwarded to the Bakersfield address — a wage-garnishment warning, which is a laugh because there's no wages to garnish on a 1099 owner-operator, but I'll have to deal with it. Fifty-two and the only thing I built was a house she lives in now with the new guy.
Fuel and the truck note in the same week again. Moved money three times to keep the fuel card live. The app flagged 'multiple small transfers.' Yeah. That's called staying on the road.

The garnishment notice keeps sitting in my head between Van Horn and Sierra Blanca. I called the number, sat on hold, hung up when the shift dispatch came in. I'll call again in Tucson. I always mean to call again in Tucson.

Downgraded LedgerSpring on April 14. Kept the free view. It tells me whether I can make the fuel card and the truck note in the same week, and that's sometimes the difference between a load and a missed load.
Balance check.

Severance ran out in February. On unemployment now and drawing down savings, which the app helpfully graphs as a line going straight down. Applied to two more roles this morning — a Capital One staff engineer, a US Bank principal. Same cover letter, swapped the top paragraph. Spouse's income covers the mortgage, thank God, but the savings drawdown is all me.

Six months since the 30% layoff took me with it. LedgerSpring's runway estimator says the savings last until roughly August at this burn. That number is the first thing I look at and the last thing I look at. People at church think I'm 'taking time.' I'm watching a line hit zero in August.
Balance check.

Cut the streaming and the gym in the app's budget tool after US Bank rejected me without an interview. Every rejection, I trim another category. The savings graph and the job spreadsheet are the same anxiety wearing two outfits.
Balance check.
Balance check.

Capital One recruiter sent a Calendly link — phone screen Tuesday. Logged the 67th application since November. Four phone screens out of 67. If this one lands, the August line stops being a countdown. If it doesn't, I start the conversation with my wife I've been avoiding about the mortgage.

Defense in 19 days. Stipend lands monthly and I live to the dollar off it. Rent split three ways in the Somerville triple-decker, utilities settled by Venmo with the roommates. About $22k in undergrad loans in deferment that I try not to think about because the second I defend, the deferment clock starts.

Opened LedgerSpring at 11:30 to check if I could cover this month's utility Venmo to my roommate and still make it to the next stipend deposit. Barely. The 'barely' is the whole story of the grad-student ledger.
Balance check.
Balance check. Login streak ended (2 days).

Sent my share of the electric bill over Venmo to the roommate. $58. That plus groceries and I'm at $90 until the stipend hits on the 1st. Computational biology PhD, fifth year, defending in three weeks, and I'm rationing to ninety dollars.
The triple-decker is loud after midnight. I ran the numbers on what happens to the $22k in loans once deferment ends and closed the app fast. Some math you do once and put away.
Downgraded LedgerSpring on the 18th. Cannot afford the premium tier on a stipend. The free tier still shows the balance, which is all I need to know whether I eat out this week (I don't).

Advisor sent edits at 11pm. I'll read them at 8 with coffee. Also the loan servicer emailed about post-graduation repayment options and I filed it, unread, in the folder of things for future-me who will hopefully have a salary.
Premium subscription downgrade confirmed. Login streak ended (1 day).
